claim: The spec's first design principle is "Cover the whole variant class, not a fixed list," and the chosen two-arm pattern is justified as matching "exactly the config spellings (`.yaml`/`.yml` variants and the bare file)." But the two arms are disjoint in a way the spec never reconciles: arm 1 requires a mandatory `.ya?ml` suffix, and arm 2's lookahead `(?![\w.\-/])` rejects anything following `config` with a `.` — which is exactly what an extensionless *variant* begins with. So `cat .faff/config.local` and `cat .faff/config-dev` (no `.yaml` suffix) match neither arm and pass the guard silently. This is not hypothetical: FAFF-1302's own overlay file is `.faff/config.local.yaml`, and an extensionless spelling of it is the most sensitive file in the set (the overlay "may hold machine-local values" per the config-under-faff-dir tests) — precisely the file a hand-read guard exists to protect. The spec's case table omits every extensionless-variant row, so the unit test it mandates will never discover the gap; the DONE item "cover the whole variant class" is asserted by prose and contradicted by the pattern.
evidence: §3 "The pattern" — arm 2 is `(?![\w.\-/])`, which cannot accept `.local`/`-dev` extensionless; the §3 case table has `cat .faff/config` (bare) but no `cat .faff/config.local` row; §1 principle "Cover the whole variant class, not a fixed list."
predicted_consequence: a `SKILL.md` line `grep slots .faff/config.local` passes the FAFF-50 guard green while hand-reading the machine-local overlay — a fail-open path in the lint for the highest-sensitivity config file, invisible to the spec's own test because the case table doesn't enumerate it.

claim: DONE requires "A `.faff/config.example.yaml` line is NOT flagged (existing `.example` line-skip)", but the §3 case table — which the DONE item says the unit test "asserts every row of" — contains no `.example` row. As specified, the test that pins the carve-out never exercises it; the carve-out's regression protection rests on scenario 5's prose only, and the spec's own "authoritative" framing of the table is undercut.
evidence: DONE item "A `.faff/config.example.yaml` line is NOT flagged"; §3 case table (no `.example` row); §4 step 3 ("asserting the §3 case table, line by line").
predicted_consequence: a build can pass the specified unit test while the `.example` line-skip has been dropped or reordered below the regex match, and the DONE item is checked off without any test deciding it.
